questions.problem: Let $A$ be a $m\times n$ matrix. What is the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $A?$
questions.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ by $A$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & ⋯ & {a}_{n} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{n}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{n} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $A$ must be $\text{Col}(A),$ the column space of $A.$

questions.problem:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Col}(A)$ for every matrix $A?$

I. $\text{Col}({A}^{T})$

II. $\text{Null}({A}^{T})$

III. $\text{Null}(A)$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Col}(A)$ consists of all linear combinations of the columns of $A$, that is, the rows of ${A}^{T}.$

If a vector is orthogonal to every linear combination of the rows of ${A}^{T},$ it must be orthogonal to each row of ${A}^{T}.$
But notice that when pre-multiplying a vector by ${A}^{T},$ we actually multiply each row of ${A}^{T}$ by that vector.
So, $\text{Col}(A)$ must be orthogonal to the left null space of $A,$ which is $\text{Null}({A}^{T}).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

**Note:** In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

questions.problem:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Null}(B)$ for every matrix $B?$

I. $\text{Null}({B}^{T})$

II. $\text{Col}(B)$

III. $\text{Col}({B}^{T})$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Null}(B)$ contains all vectors that, when pre-multiplied by $B,$ result in the zero-vector $0.$ 

When pre-multiplying a vector by $B,$ we actually multiply each row of $B$ by that vector. So, $\text{Null}(B)$ must be orthogonal to the row space of $B,$ which is $\text{Col}({A}^{T}).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

**Note:** In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $B$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

questions.problem:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Col}(XY)$ for all compatible matrices $X$ and $Y?$

I. $\text{Null}({Y}^{T}\,{X}^{T})$

II. $\text{Col}({Y}^{T}\,{X}^{T})$

III. $\text{Null}(XY)$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Col}(XY)$ consists of all linear combinations of the columns of $XY$, that is, the rows of $(XY)^{T}={Y}^{T}\,{X}^{T}.$

If a vector is orthogonal to every linear combination of the rows of ${Y}^{T}\,{X}^{T},$ it must be orthogonal to each row of ${Y}^{T}\,{X}^{T}.$
But notice that when pre-multiplying a vector by ${Y}^{T}\,{X}^{T},$ we actually multiply each row of ${Y}^{T}\,{X}^{T}$ by that vector.
So, $\text{Col}(XY)$ must be orthogonal to the left null space of $XY,$ which is $\text{Null}({Y}^{T}\,{X}^{T}).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

**Note:** In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.
